headline: Even Bull's cheaper-entry plan is a coin flip: the first goal pays too little for a 60% hit rate, the stop is one normal hour away, and the price is stretched under today's high.

messages.text: Fair play to Bull for dropping the 'buy right now' idea. But I'll go through his plan point by point, and the desk numbers don't back it.

messages.reply_to: Bull: First goal is 158.83, just under today's high
messages.text: That first goal only pays 0.65 for every 1 risked. To break even you would need to win about 61 times in 100, and the desk's replays give 60. That is a coin flip that costs spread, not an edge.
The bigger goal at 159.00 is hit before the safety exit only about 33 times in 100. And the typical ending price, 158.66, is below Bull's own entry of 158.72.

messages.reply_to: Bull: exit at 158.55, just under a spot where price has turned 3 times
messages.text: That spot, 158.574, is an old ceiling, not a guaranteed floor. A stop only 0.17 away is just 1.07 times a normal hour's move, so a regular wiggle can reach it. Also 158.768 is a ceiling sitting just above his entry.

messages.reply_to: Bull: price sits above its 9, 21 and 50-period averages
messages.text: Uptrend yes, but the 1-hour RSI of 76 means very stretched. The 5-minute and 15-minute charts show the push fading (both MACD readings, a momentum gauge, are negative), and even the 1-hour one is shrinking.

messages.reply_to: Bull: US inflation came in hotter than expected
messages.text: That news came out at about 15:16 UTC, hours ago, and the dollar already jumped (+0.7%). Waiting for a dip to 158.72 means buying only if the push is already failing. A 10-year bond sale at 18:00 UTC could move yields either way.

messages.reply_to: Bull: the desk's odds test says there is no strong edge
messages.text: I accept the correction: my 26% was the optimizer's plan, not Bull's. But Bull's own plan comes out at -0.004R on average, so at best break-even, and no plan the code tried has real edge. I'd skip.

argument:
Correction first: my Round 1 odds (26.5% target-first) were the optimizer's plan, not Bull's. The desk replayed Bull's actual plan (entry 158.72, stop 158.55, targets 158.83 and 159.00) 10,000 times: first target before stop 60.4%, stop first 39.6%, average -0.004R. Because target 1 pays only 0.647R gross (0.11 of reward vs 0.17 of risk), break-even needs about 61% wins. It gets 60%, so the expected value is zero before spread and slippage. Real history is similar (33 target, 19 stop, 7 neither of 59), but that is one sample per day. Target 2 (159.00, 1.647R) is reached before the stop only 32.6% of replays, and the median replay ends at 158.66, below the entry.

Bull's level logic is thin. The stop at 158.55 sits under a 3x swing high (158.574), but a level where price turned before is not a floor, and the stop is 1.07 x the 1h ATR (0.159), only about one normal hour. A 1x swing high at 158.768 sits just above the entry and today's high 158.847 is basically target 1, so the first goal pays 0.11 into a ceiling. 'No listed ceiling above today's high' is an absence in a short-history file, not support; StoneX's seven-week resistance headline (snippet only) points the other way.

Momentum: 1h RSI 76.1 is stretched, 15m is 70.3, and the 5m and 15m MACD histograms are negative; the 1h histogram is positive but falling (0.0887 to 0.0843). The CPI catalyst is hours old and the dollar index is already +0.7%. A limit fill at 158.72 happens only if price dips, which means the push is failing: adverse selection (my reasoning, not a desk figure). The 10-year note auction at 18:00 UTC adds yield risk, and Bull himself called the yield spike reversible. Optimizer: NO_EDGE; context only NEUTRAL.

evidence.claim: Live USD/JPY 158.79, day high 158.85, day low 157.86; 1h RSI 76.1, 15m RSI 70.3, 5m RSI 58.8; 5m and 15m MACD histograms negative (-0.0084, -0.0052); 1h histogram +0.0843, down from +0.0887
evidence.plain: Price still sits at today's top, the long chart is stretched, and the push is fading on the short charts and slightly on the 1-hour one.

evidence.claim: Desk Time Machine on Bull's plan: first target before stop 60.4%, stop first 39.6%, average -0.004R; first target pays only 0.647R, so it needs about 61% wins to break even
evidence.plain: Even on Bull's own plan the desk calls it a coin flip: the odds are about equal to what the small reward needs, so there is no edge.

evidence.claim: Second target 159.00 reached before the stop only 32.6% of replays; median finish 158.66 (below the 158.72 entry), 5th to 95th percentile 158.06 to 159.24
evidence.plain: The bigger goal Bull needs for a good payout is hit about one time in three, and the typical ending price is below Bull's entry.

evidence.claim: Plan check: stop 158.55 is 0.17 away (1.07 x 1h ATR 0.159), entry is 0.5 ATR from the live price, reward to target 1 is 0.11 (0.647R) and to target 2 is 0.28 (1.647R) before costs
evidence.plain: The stop is only about one normal hour of movement away, and the first goal is smaller than that.

evidence.claim: Levels above Bull's entry 158.72: 1x swing high 158.768, today's high 158.847. Levels near the stop: 3x swing high 158.574, Pivot R2 158.686, Pivot R1 158.489, 1x swing high 158.503
evidence.plain: A ceiling (158.768) sits just above Bull's entry, and today's high is right at his first goal. His 'floor' for the stop is an old ceiling that held only because price turned there before.

evidence.claim: Optimizer NO_EDGE: 12 plans pass the cost rule, none passes the odds test; best target-first 26.5%, stop-first 66.6%, avg -0.099R (history 10 targets, 33 stops of 59)
evidence.plain: Code searched 24 plans and found none worth taking. This is a different plan than Bull's, which I corrected from Round 1.

evidence.claim: Event guard CLEAR but 10-year US note auction (Medium impact, tier 3) at 18:00 UTC, about 10 minutes after the snapshot; US 10-year yield 5.015% (+3.1%) and dollar index +0.7% today; context verdict NEUTRAL
evidence.plain: A government bond sale, which can swing yields and the dollar, lands right as Bull wants his order sitting; the yield spike he called reversible is the very driver of the dollar's move.

evidence.claim: Hot US CPI puts 50 bp Fed hike in play (published 15:16 UTC, 2.6h before snapshot); StoneX headline: seven-week USD/JPY resistance standoff (08:23 UTC, snippet only)
evidence.plain: The inflation news is hours old and already in the price; a headline says sellers have held this zone for weeks (I only saw the headline).
evidence.source: news.json (FXStreet tier 2; StoneX via Google News, snippet only)

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: buy a dip at 158.72, first goal 158.83, then 159.00
rebuttals.response: Desk: 60.4% target-first vs 61% needed for 0.647R; avg -0.004R. Second target 32.6%. No edge.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: stop 158.55 sits just under a 3x swing high so it is protected
rebuttals.response: Old turning points are not guarantees; stop is 1.07 x 1h ATR, inside a normal hour's range; 158.768 ceiling is above entry.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: 1h EMAs stacked up, RSI 76, buyers in control
rebuttals.response: RSI 76.1 is stretched; 5m/15m MACD negative; 1h MACD histogram falling 0.0887 to 0.0843.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: hot CPI and Waller push the dollar up, DXY +0.7%
rebuttals.response: CPI was published 15:16 UTC, already priced; context verdict NEUTRAL; 10y auction at 18:00 UTC adds risk.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: optimizer's test used a different plan
rebuttals.response: Accepted and corrected; Bull's plan is still only break-even in the desk replay and the optimizer found no plan with edge.

plan_flaws: Target 1 pays 0.647R gross; break-even needs about 61% wins, desk gives 60.4%, avg -0.004R
Target 2 (159.00) before stop only 32.6%; median replay end 158.66 below entry 158.72
Stop 158.55 is 1.07x 1h ATR from entry, inside normal noise
Target 1 (158.83) is 0.11 above entry and basically at today's high 158.847; 1x swing high 158.768 sits between entry and target
Limit entry needs a dip, so fills come when momentum is already fading (5m/15m MACD negative)
10-year note auction at 18:00 UTC inside the window; event guard CLEAR but not empty
plan_flaws_plain: The first profit goal pays less than the risk and needs the desk's 60% hit rate to reach just break-even.
The bigger 159.00 goal is hit only about one time in three.
The safety exit is about one normal hour of movement away, so an ordinary wiggle can hit it.
The first goal is squeezed under today's high, with a small ceiling at 158.77 in the way.
The order fills only if price slips, which is when buyers are already tiring.
A US bond sale at 18:00 UTC can jolt the dollar right as the order is live.
conditions_to_reconsider: Reconsider if price closes an hour above today's high of 158.85 and holds, with the 1-hour RSI cooled back toward 60, or if a plan is found whose first goal pays at least 1R at the same stop distance and still reaches target first about 50% in the desk replay.
